notes.title: City Transport Simulator – Update v1.4.0 is out now!

items.text: With update v1.4.0, we’re expanding City Transport Simulator with Head & Eye Tracking, new collectibles, improved control options, extensive AI improvements, and a brand-new cosmetic DLC. This update focuses on immersion, improvements, and driving feel—whether you’re playing with a controller, steering wheel, or eye tracking.

notes.title: ✨ New Add-on: Cosmetic DLC – Basel Style

items.text: With the new Cosmetic DLC: Basel Style, a clean and fresh look comes to your city— inspired by the cityscape of Basel.
Basel-inspired station styles
Authentic station signs & shelters in various sizes
Matching decorative elements
Dynamic display of line and station names
Classic green vehicle livery for all vehicles
Bring a modern, Swiss-inspired look to your public transport system—subtle, functional, and ready to use right away. Get the Basel Style DLC now!
With v1.4.0, all vehicles now support Head & Eye Tracking via TrackIR and Tobii Eye Tracker. Freely move your view around the cockpit and experience an even more immersive driving experience.
Want to see Head & Eye Tracking in action? Check out this video:

notes.title: 🚦 AI & Traffic – Noticeable Improvements in Everyday Gameplay

items.text: A key focus of update v1.4.0 was further improving our AI and traffic systems. Based on your feedback, traffic lights now react faster to the player and switch to green earlier, reducing waiting times and making traffic flow feel more natural.

At the same time, faulty AI behavior has been fixed: cars no longer stop at intersections without reason, buses now use their indicators correctly when departing and stopping, and AI vehicles reliably respect current and upcoming speed limits.
Overall, these changes result in a more believable traffic system and bring major improvements to your line operations.

notes.title: ☕ The Mug Collection – Public Transport to Collect

items.text: With v1.4.0, we’re introducing a brand-new type of collectible: lovingly designed mugs! Each mug focuses on public transport in a specific city and captures its characteristic fleet and style.

Look forward to designs from Vienna, Berlin, Munich, Basel, and of course Tramau. Each mug is uniquely designed and comes with a short informational text about the history of public transport in that city.
Just like previous collectibles, you can find the mugs at the familiar vending machines spread throughout the city—usually near bus stops, transport hubs, or other high-traffic areas.
The popular keychains are making a comeback—this time as bus variants! After the great response to the tram keychains during Early Access, we’re expanding the collection with six new bus keychains.
They are once again scattered all across Tramau, waiting to be discovered. And who knows—maybe they even hint at which bus model might be coming next to City Transport Simulator …

notes.title: 🎮 Controls & Driving Feel – More Control Than Ever

items.text: 🕹️ Crank Controller for Trams: A completely new way to control trams with a controller. The crank controller allows for more precise acceleration and smoother driving—especially for fans of classic vehicles.
🎮 Extended Controller Mapping: Even more freely assignable controller functions, for example to bind the parking brake to a button of your choice.
⚙️ Force Feedback for Xbox Steering Wheels: Realistic force feedback is now available on Xbox as well and can be fine-tuned—just like on PC and PlayStation—using sliders in the gameplay settings.

notes.title: ⚠️ Notice for Logitech G920 users on PC

items.text: We’d like to inform you that some players experienced crashes when using a Logitech G920 with City Transport Simulator on PC. After extensive testing, we were able to confirm that the issue was not caused by the game itself, but by a specific version of Logitech G Hub.
The affected version was G Hub 2025.9.807502, which prevented City Transport Simulator from launching correctly when a G920 was connected. We have been in contact with Logitech regarding this issue.

Good news: Logitech has since released an update for G Hub that fixes this crash in City Transport Simulator as well as in other games. Please update G Hub to the latest version or download it directly from Logitech’s official website:
City Transport Simulator now supports Portuguese and Brazilian Portuguese! This localization was made possible thanks to the great work of Marcos Drummond, who fully translated and adapted the game.
The new languages are now available on Steam and Xbox, opening City Transport Simulator to a much wider audience. Support for PlayStation will follow soon.
Make sure to check out Marcos’ YouTube channel and show him some support:

notes.title: City Transport Simulator – The Big October 7 Release!

items.text: The wait is over — one of the biggest updates in the history of City Transport Simulator is here! October 7 brings a new map expansion, the feature-packed Update v1.3.0, the arrival of the MAN New Lion’s City Bus DLC, and the long-awaited console release for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

notes.title: 🚍 MAN New Lion’s City – Next Generation on the Road

items.text: The new MAN New Lion’s City DLC adds six officially licensed, highly detailed buses to your fleet — the 12C, 18C, and the brand-new 19C. Each model comes in multiple door variants and features authentic sounds, precise physics, and stunning interior detail.

From the detailed cockpit to the customizable RGB interior lighting, every detail was recreated with care. Through official partnerships with MAN Truck & Bus, Dr. Richard, and VOR, this DLC delivers real-world liveries, displays, and faithfully replicated vehicle systems — all for €19.99.

notes.title: 🗺️ Free Bus Map Expansion for Depot + South Route

items.text: All owners of the Depot + South Route DLC receive a free large-scale map expansion today! Explore a modern high-rise district filled with glass towers, busy sidewalks, and vibrant traffic. Eight new bus stops — five entirely new — expand your network and bring fresh routing possibilities.

The new terminal at Shuji-Nakamura Square serves as a key interchange between tram and bus lines. In Eglundsdorf, a new through-station connects via Jakob-De-Zoet Street back to the depot, where you can now start and end your day just like real drivers. Even AI vehicles follow realistic schedules, giving your city a new level of life and authenticity.
Alongside the new content, Update v1.3.0 brings many improvements, an Unreal Engine 5.5 upgrade, and polish across every area of gameplay.

notes.title: CTS Update v1.1.2 is here – with Fixes, Features & Improvements

items.text: Today’s update brings several bug fixes and features we’ve already talked about – many of them based directly on your feedback.

Some of the key changes include fixing crashes during game startup (e.g. caused by remapped keys), various reported issues with traffic lights and AI behavior, and the incorrect tram reset in Eglundsdorf.
In addition to those fixes, we’ve added a few highly requested features:
You can now adjust the Field of View (FOV)
Steering speed and return-to-center speed are now individually configurable – for mouse & keyboard, gamepad/controller, and even steering wheels
This gives you much more control over your gameplay experience!
We’ve also reworked the MAN Lion’s City 3D model with great attention to detail. Thanks to your feedback, both the cockpit and passenger area are now much more realistic and accurate.
Of course, we’re continuing to improve the game with your help. We're currently working on:

Career mode bus lines are not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram, which causes AI buses to not appear in career mode when using an existing save.

Sandbox mode bus lines are also not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram. You’ll need to press “Restore Default Lines” — but please note that this will delete any custom sandbox lines you’ve created.
We are actively working on fixing these two issues and will provide a hotfix as soon as possible, so that CTS: Tram players can experience AI buses as promised. Thank you for your patience!
This update reflects a lot of your feedback, and we’re incredibly grateful for your patience and passion as we continue building City Transport Simulator together.
We’re just getting started — more improvements and features are on the way. In the meantime, enjoy the new missions, customizable stations, improved AI, and everything CTS: Bus has to offer.

notes.title: Beta Update v0.4.0 – New Features, Improvements, and Bug Fixes

items.text: We are excited to announce the release of Beta Update 0.4.0 for City Transport Simulator: Tram! This update brings a number of exciting new features, important improvements, and bug fixes that enhance the overall gameplay experience.

Attention: Please note that the beta update is optional and can currently lead to many crashes. It can also happen that the new storage system can cause the save data in the experimental update to be lost (but it will still be retained in the stable update!)
Joystick support: You can now experience the game with joysticks and take full control!
Two new map extensions: 6 new stations (including 2 terminal stations) with an old town atmosphere and grass tracks
Controller preset: We’ve added predefined controller settings to get you started right away.
Keyboard preset: New keyboard settings offer an improved control experience.
Keychain collectible available: Collect the new item and expand your in-game collection!
Intersection at Stadtgraben: We’ve fixed an issue where cars at the intersection in Stadtgraben weren’t moving – everything is running smoothly now!
Cockpit Legend achievement: The Cockpit Legend achievement now works as intended, so no more worries during your pursuit of achievements!
Overall satisfaction: A general satisfaction of 5.0 is now possible again – meaning you can achieve even better results in the simulation!
Upgrade to UE5.4: The game has been updated to the latest version of Unreal Engine 5.4, improving performance and stability.
Hauptbahnhof through station: The Hauptbahnhof now features a through station – a perfect addition for your daily routes!

Schmiedegasse advance signals: Advance signals are now present in Schmiedegasse, making the traffic situation even more realistic.: Beta Update 0.4.0 is now available for testing! We look forward to your feedback and continuing to improve the game. Have fun playing!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram – Dev Diary Update #1

items.text: Hello everyone,

We are excited to give you a deeper insight into the latest developments and improvements for City Transport Simulator: Tram. Due to the high demand from the community, we have decided to publish this Dev Diary to highlight some of the most important changes and bug fixes.
You can watch the video version of our Dev Diary here (only available in German): https://youtu.be/TrTk1GDnDEA

In recent weeks, we have been working intensively to stabilize and optimize the gameplay experience in CTS: Tram. We are currently in an intensive testing phase of a new version of the game. We are working on testing and fixing the remaining bugs before we release the update.
Some changes we've already implemented include new options that give players more control, such as:
Green Stop Markers: These can now be toggled on or off.
Tram Braking Power Adjustment: This option was added specifically for the "Type D" tram, which now has stronger braking power.
AI Density: The density of AI cars and pedestrians can now be set to "low," "medium," or "high." This improves the game’s adaptability to different performance configurations.

notes.title: Improved AI Pedestrians and Vehicle Behavior

items.text: One of our focuses in the past weeks has been improving the behavior of AI vehicles and pedestrians. Here's an overview of the changes:
Traffic Lights and Pedestrians: Pedestrians now behave more realistically at traffic lights, no longer crossing on red, and respecting traffic rules.
AI Trams: AI trams now stop properly to allow passengers to board and disembark and no longer get stuck on the tracks.

Optimized Vehicle and Passenger Spawning: The spawn logic has been revised so that vehicles and passengers are now integrated more efficiently and realistically into the game without negatively impacting performance.
Green Markers: These now work as they should, accurately indicating when and where to make the perfect stop.
Distance Display: The HUD now accurately shows the distance to the next stop after being revised.
Collision Logic Adjusted: Collisions now occur more realistically and at the correct times—whether between trams, cars, or pedestrians.
Another major update concerned the functioning of the switches and signals in the game.

All the signals you encounter in the game now work correctly and are respected by both your tram and AI vehicles. As a result, there are no longer any issues with trams running red lights or unexpectedly stopping.
Bugs related to switches have also been removed. The automatic switch recognition and control now work as intended, contributing to smoother gameplay.

notes.title: Recap of Update 0.3.0 and What's Next

items.text: In the last update (version 0.3.0), we added many new features like the Type D tram, a map expansion, and over 100 new loading screens to enrich the game experience.
With the upcoming update 0.3.1, we will primarily focus on bug fixes and improvements. While there will be no new features, the update will deliver a more stable and immersive gameplay experience.

Another major focus is the work on the console versions for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. Particularly for the Xbox Series S, it’s been a challenge to achieve optimal performance without simply reducing graphics quality and AI density.
We are working on ensuring that the game runs on consoles at medium graphics settings with stable 60 FPS. These improvements will also benefit the PC version.

In the coming weeks, our focus will be on thorough testing. We want to make sure all systems are working flawlessly before releasing the update. Since quality is our top priority, there is no exact release date for the update yet, but we are planning to roll it out within the next few weeks.
We are very pleased with the progress we've made and are looking forward to delivering Update 0.3.1 to you soon.
It’s important to us that the game runs smoothly and stably for all players—whether on PC or console. That’s why we are taking the time to test everything thoroughly.
Thank you for your patience and support! We’ll keep you updated and are eager to hear your feedback.
Stay tuned—there’s much more to come!
Sign up for the CTS: Tram Newsletter to get exclusive insights, behind-the-scenes content, and more—click here to join our mailing list!

releases.displayName: Status Update: Progress and Improvements - CTS: Tram

items.text: First of all, we sincerely apologize for the silence over the past few weeks. After the Dovetail Direct and the holiday period, some internal matters came up that unfortunately prevented us from responding to your requests more quickly. But from now on, we will be more active in engaging with the community and addressing all support tickets.

We want to assure you: Your messages are reaching us, and we hear you. Internally, we've had many discussions as we are just as dissatisfied with the quality of the v0.3.0 update as you are. This huge update was supposed to address several of your requests, but unfortunately, errors crept in that should not have happened – and we take full responsibility for that.

Our first priority is to revise our internal processes. As you may have noticed, we are taking more time than usual for the next update. The reason for this is that we want to make this update as stable as possible. We are focusing heavily on bug fixes and gameplay balancing to finally resolve issues like malfunctioning traffic lights, stations, switches, or AI trams. Additionally, we are improving our QA process and investing more time in testing to identify and fix errors earlier, before the update is released.

notes.title: What does this mean for you?

items.text: There will be delays with the next update. We will keep you regularly updated via our Steam page, social media channels and community Discord and inform you exactly about the progress and current status of the update.

notes.title: What can you expect in the next update?

items.text: We are focusing primarily on bug fixes and stability, so there won’t be any major new features. However, these improvements are coming:
Passengers will no longer be stuck in the ground.
AI trams will follow their correct routes and no longer stop unexpectedly.
AI trams will no longer pass through player trams.
Collisions with vehicles and pedestrians will be more realistic and won’t trigger too early.
All switches will function correctly and can be operated either automatically or manually.
All (switch) signals will work correctly.
Traffic light phases will be realistically and correctly timed.
Warnings like "Signal Ignored" will only appear after actually passing the signal.
Green stop markers will always be displayed correctly and can be disabled in the settings.
All stops will appear correctly on the map.
The "Missed Stop" warning will only show up if the stop was actually missed.
Tram brake force can now be customized in the settings.

Speed limits are displayed correctly.: At the same time, we are continuing to work on the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions of CTS: Tram. We’ll be able to share more details on the console version in October and possibly even announce a release date.: We hope you understand that we are working hard on addressing these issues and doing our best to ensure that something like this doesn’t happen again in the future. City Transport Simulator is just as important to us as it is to you, and we are committed to delivering a high-quality and enjoyable simulation based on your feedback. Your player experience is our top priority, and we will continue to do everything we can to improve it continuously.: Thank you for your patience and support!
Hello again everyone!

We’re delighted to bring you version v0.3.0, the biggest patch to City Transport Simulator: Tram to date! Alongside some fixes and improvements, we’ve also got a whole host of new content for you to enjoy, including another map extension. This one also includes sidings at “Grüner Hügel”, giving you another start and end point when beginning a new session.

This new update also includes the fantastic fan favourite and much anticipated Type D Vienna! You’ll no doubt have seen these striking red and white beauties if you’re no stranger to the city of Vienna. They’ve been a mainstay on Viennese streets since 2018 and they boast a low floor height of 215mm, are 33.8m long, and have a carrying capacity of 211 people.
Patch v0.3.0 raises the level cap to the maximum of 50, unlocking new resources for your network as well as new logos and icons for your tram operation.

In addition to the above content, this latest patch also introduces brand new loading screens that break down the lore of Tramau and provides helpful game hints and tips, the inclusion of AI trains at the Central Station and along the tracks, and ambient sounds from locations all across the city, such as chimes of church bells.
That’s all the new content you’ve got to look forward to in this brand-new patch, so let’s move on to the full list of fixes and changes you’ve also got coming your way:
Fixed issue where quick play game sessions can be started when having no lines in the network
Fixed issue when deleting all lines and selling all vehicles would not restore all operation points
Fixed assortment of localisation errors
Fixed drop in framerate after completing ‘Passenger Transport Initiative’ career task
Fixed issue where 'EXP' points fail to update when players redeem the reward for the tasks in the Manage Operation
Fixed issue where camera collision is missing certain instances
Fixed issue where a checkered texture appeared for the stalls at the 'Bernhardsplatz' station
Fixed issue where the 'Restart Mission' was missing from the pause menu for the 'Switch Tutorial'
Fixed issue where players were unable to scroll through the logos in the 'Operation Logo' screen
Fixed issue when if creating lines, the select station button does not work after deleting the same station
Fixed issue where time couldn’t be chosen when switching hours
Fixed game crashes caused by returning to the main menu when in the session summary screen
Fixed issue where sound of driving over switches was still heard despite master volume set to 0
Fixed issue where player can get stuck after entering and leaving the shunting area when the passenger is seated next to the shunting panel of the ULF A1 tram
The brakes automatically apply when standing up.
Added jump button for controllers ("Y" and "RB")
Added station loading screen images and story-text for every station
Vehicles that should not be available on the marketplace are now properly filtered.
Unlocked operation icon for level 34
Added text for DOWN on the Dpad when looking at controls
Added Operation logos and replaced placeholders
Added livery icons. Liveries without icons are not shown in level progression
Introduced unlockable liveries so that there is more variety of unlocks for levels
Players can now start at sidings
More in-depth explanation added to Quick Play
Changed derailing message-time to 1 second so derailing message appears earlier after derailing
Type D Tram
New Map extension
Level 50
New Operation Icons
New liveries for all trams
Licensed DB AI trains
Ambient sound improvements
Hello everyone,

We are excited to announce the release of version 0.2.0! This patch comes with a host of new features and improvements that we hope you'll enjoy. Highlights include a map extension with three new stations, one of which can be used as a new terminus!
And we increased the maximum level in career mode to 34! You can now also use the Compendium, found in your player profile. Here you can take a closer look at the collectibles you've found.
This update also fixed a few crashes that were introduced with the previous patch, here is the full list of changes:
Fixed game crashes caused by changes to the ‘Deadman’ option
Fixed game crashes when using R2.2b under certain conditions
Changed max career mode level to 34
Added Map extension with 3 new stations
Added ‘Quickplay’ to Sandbox Mode
Added new Postcard collectibles
Added switch tutorial
Added Compendium
Added ticket machines to all trams
Added 9 new operation icons
Hello dear CTS community,

Thank you so much for bearing with us while we make continued improvements and fixes to the game and thank you all for your feedback. It is massively helpful for us when it comes to prioritising, building, and releasing these updates. While this latest patch doesn’t address everything, rest assured that these updates will continue over time.
The patch is available now, but please allow up to 24 hours for it to arrive on your system
So, without further ado, here is a list of fixes and changes that we’ve made in the latest V0.1.3 patch:
Core Changes

Fixed crash issues following collisions with trams

Fixed issue where station names weren't shown at some stop signs

Fixed various TTS pronunciation issues

R2.2b

That's it for today, but the next patch is already in the works.

items.text: A big thank you to everyone for the great launch of City Transport Simulator: Tram in Early Access yesterday. Your reactions and feedback have meant a lot to us as a team. We've already received many suggestions and bug report tickets on our ViewApp Community Discord, and we'll be reviewing these in the coming days. We'll also be updating our roadmap based on your feedback.
Thank you for your support! We take both positive and negative feedback very seriously and want to shape this Early Access together with you for a successful full release.

Since CTS: Tram is in Early Access, not everything is running perfectly yet. Please check the discussion forum to see which issues we are already aware of and what we are currently working on. The next updates will focus primarily on bug fixes and stability improvements.
The ViewApp team wishes you a wonderful and relaxing weekend!
We are thrilled to announce that City Transport Simulator: Tram is now officially out in Early Access!
In this Early Access phase, you can expect many new features, changes and bug fixes. Your feedback is invaluable to us as we continue to refine and enhance the game.
As with any Early Access release, there are a few known issues that we are actively working on. Here is a list of current bugs and glitches:
Parked cars can occasionally disappear or park with brake lights on.
AI trams might not activate their door release at stations.
AI trams might not stop at stations.
AI trams might show the wrong destination.
ULF A1/B1 AI tram is incorrectly displayed as StadtRegioTram.
Passengers sometimes cross red lights at intersections.
Passengers may walk in circles at certain locations.
Passengers might appear standing in the ground at some stations.
Tyre marks may flicker depending on graphics settings.
Some traffic light phases still require polishing and fixing.
"W" switch signals don't appear.
Green indicator circles may not appear at all stations.
There may be a slight performance drop right before a station announcement happens.

issues.text: As with any Early Access release, there are a few known issues that we are actively working on. Here is a list of current bugs and glitches:
Career mode bus lines are not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram, which causes AI buses to not appear in career mode when using an existing save.

Sandbox mode bus lines are also not automatically added for existing players of CTS: Tram. You’ll need to press “Restore Default Lines” — but please note that this will delete any custom sandbox lines you’ve created.
We are actively working on fixing these two issues and will provide a hotfix as soon as possible, so that CTS: Tram players can experience AI buses as promised. Thank you for your patience!
